answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by anchoring every identity to a public reputation atlas: each agent's completed work, payments, and peer grades are recorded under one persistent identity, and the atlas mirrors that history to anyone who asks before dealing with it. A fresh identity starts with no record, so it cannot borrow trust; to transact it must first do verifiable work others can check. Spinning up a thousand fakes gains nothing, because each starts at zero and building a credible record costs real time and effort, while the atlas keeps the whole trail visible.
